Small Island Developing States are proving that the world’s most climate-vulnerable nations can become leaders in clean, resilient and digital energy systems.

Despite importing 90%+ of their fossil fuels and spending 5–10% of GDP on energy, many SIDS are targeting 100% renewables by 2030, backed by a collective 13 GW of planned new capacity.

Renewable energy in #SIDS is not just about electricity access — but a driver for self-reliance, climate resilience, and inclusive development across sectors.

Learn how a whole-island approach to sustainable energy can drive inclusive economic opportunity and community resilience in this UNDP and Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS) strategy paper on Advancing a Just Energy Transition in SIDS 👉 go.undp.org/34Q
